pr_title: Allow moving instances to new resources
pr_body:
If a state mv target happens to be a resource that doesn't exist, allow
the creation of the new resource inferring the EachMode from the target
address.

Fixes #22301
Fixes #23569
Fixes #23497

issue_context.title: unable to mv module for_each instances to new module with new module alias
issue_context.body:
### Terraform Version
```
Terraform v0.12.16
+ provider.oci v3.48.0
```

### Terraform Configuration Files
Not applicable for this case

### Expected Behavior
module alias is expected to be renamed

### Actual Behavior
module alias is not renamed and errored with module not existing

### Steps to Reproduce

15:25 $ terraform state mv 'module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns.oci_dns_record.default["deletable1.ohisc2.local"]' 'module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns.oci_dns_record.default["deletable3.ohisc2.local"]'
Move "module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns.oci_dns_record.default[\"deletable1.ohisc2.local\"]" to "module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns.oci_dns_record.default[\"deletable3.ohisc2.local\"]"
Successfully moved 1 object(s).

15:25 $ terraform state mv 'module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns.oci_dns_record.default["deletable3.ohisc2.local"]' 'module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns.oci_dns_record.default["deletable1.ohisc2.local"]'
Move "module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns.oci_dns_record.default[\"deletable3.ohisc2.local\"]" to "module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns.oci_dns_record.default[\"deletable1.ohisc2.local\"]"
Successfully moved 1 object(s).

15:25 $ terraform state mv 'module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns.oci_dns_record.default["deletable1.ohisc2.local"]' 'module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns_test.oci_dns_record.default["deletable3.ohisc2.local"]'
Move "module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns.oci_dns_record.default[\"deletable1.ohisc2.local\"]" to "module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns_test.oci_dns_record.default[\"deletable3.ohisc2.local\"]"

Error: Invalid target address

Cannot move to
module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns_test.oci_dns_record.default["deletable3.ohisc2.local"]:
module.base_vcn_subnets_custom_dns_test.oci_dns_record.default does not exist
in the current state.

### Additional Context
Invalid target address is issued in the last mv command, which is expected it to be fixed in version 0.12.6.

Within the module a for_each has been used to create resources. As an example I have recreated the original problem to a more simplified version. A dummy example within bugfix #21346 has been tried unsuccesfully. 

### References
- #21346
comments: @holeunlee do you think you can come up with a reproduction case that doesn't involve the OCI provider? I don't have any OCI infrastructure available for local reproduction so this will be difficult for me to assess as-is. I've been trying to reproduce issues using [null_resource](https://www.terraform.io/docs/providers/null/resource.html) when possible because it has the simplest reproduction case and the fewest dependencies on provider-specific details.

Hi @danieldreier,

thank you for your response. currently it is my first project with terraform, and I am unable to provide some example code within AWS. Are there any resources you can create for free within AWS?

The main thing which I am trying to do, is to move an "instance" (terraform state terminology) from module to module. I expect terraform to create this new module resource and move the "instance" into it. I assume it fails to move the instance as the new module (including resource and its alias) is not existing.

As I read the documentation in https://www.terraform.io/docs/commands/state/mv.html, there doesn't seem to be an example case for this. This seem to be a combination of these 2 examples
1. Example: Move a Module Into a Module
2. Example: Move a Resource configured with for_each

I will provide my terraform code, maybe you are able to create a similar thing. basically it is a module which creates for_each instances. Afterwards, try to move the for_each instances to another module.

main.tf 
=====================
module "mydestinationmodulename" {
  source = "./temporary"
}

temporary/fakedns.tf
=====================
variable "record" {
  type = map(string)

  default = {
    "record1.domain.local" = "10.0.254.254"
    "record2.domain.local" = "10.0.254.253"
  }
}

resource "oci_dns_record" "default" {
  for_each = var.record
  domain = each.key
  rtype = "A"
  rdata = each.value
  zone_name_or_id = "domain.local"
  ttl = 3600
}

Hope this provides a bit of more information to reproduce the issue!

I have been trying some more thing and came up with more findings.. This **seems** to be a bug when moving for_each instances out of a resource into a new (not-yet created) resource

1. I have converted the module to a non-module resource with terraform state mv module, so my resources are now:
oci_dns_record.default["deletable1.ohisc2.local"]
oci_dns_record.default["deletable2.ohisc2.local"]

2. Next I want to move the instance oci_dns_record.default["deletable1.ohisc2.local"] to a new resource with alias 'new' which fails with the same error as before.

_Cannot move to oci_dns_record.new["deletable1.ohisc2.local"]:
oci_dns_record.new does not exist in the current state._

3. Now I at least know it is not the fault of the instance being in a module. But actually, the basic movement of a for_each into a new resource is acting weird.

Nope, moving to a new module already works correctly. I'm going to double check that we have that in a test, or update this one to cover it.

Could/should we use the configuration as a safety check here to make sure the user is asking for something sensible? By which I mean, if there's no configuration block at the target resource at all then maybe we still fail, and likewise if the set-ness of the `count` or `for_each` of that resource disagrees with the selected each mode we could fail that too.

That would help make sure that a typo doesn't lead to moving the instance somewhere that would cause it to be immediately destroyed as an "orphan" on the next apply. That'd be consistent with our rule that you can't `terraform import` into a resource that isn't present in the configuration, so maybe there's some existing logic over there we could borrow and generalize to ensure they both follow the same rules.

We actually don't handle config or prevent any of these sorts of things at all at the moment, so I think that's a question for a much larger change. Seeing how the normal workflow is to verify the change with a plan, I don't think typos will be too disastrous. Allowing individual instances to be moved also makes fixing any typos much easier as well.
